name: AutoClip
one_liner: Drop in a long video and AI finds the highlights, cutting captioned short clips automatically.

text.why: Finding the watchable moments in a long interview, lecture or stream replay is tedious work. AutoClip reads the subtitles and audio with AI, scores highlights, writes titles, and cuts captioned short clips and compilations automatically.
text.take: Plenty of tools promise AI video editing; being able to pick desktop, web or CLI from one project, and swap the model provider freely, is the practical part.
build: Available as a desktop app (Mac/Windows), a Docker web UI, or a CLI/MCP pipeline. Feed it a local file or a YouTube/Bilibili link, it prepares subtitles, scores highlight segments with your choice of model (Qwen, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Gemini, or a local Ollama/LM Studio model), and cuts clips. Direct publishing to TikTok, YouTube Shorts and more shipped in v1.3.2.

who.role: Content creators who need short clips out of interviews, lectures or stream replays, and podcasters looking to cut editing time.

start.text: Download the Mac or Windows build from GitHub Releases, add an API key for your chosen model in settings, and import a video.

caveat: AI analysis needs an API key from a model provider such as Qwen or OpenAI (a local Ollama model is free). The interface defaults to Chinese, but has supported 8 languages including Korean since v1.3.1.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
